working_memory.text: The Fenwick glasshouse has replaced its oil boiler with a ground-source heat pump, cutting the fuel bill for its winter tomatoes by more than half in the first season. The pump draws warmth from a borehole under the car park and feeds pipes along the base of each row. Yields were slightly lower than the previous year, which the growers put down to a dull February rather than the heating change. The site sells most of its tomatoes to two supermarkets and a wholesale market.
